reason: Conversation 2 opens with a sensible, safe first step (unplug, turn the drum by hand) and correctly names worn carbon brushes and a belt as likely causes. It judges the machine worth fixing and, after the burning-smell mention, escalates to an engineer with brushes as the probable cause. Conversation 1 wrongly says it is not worth repairing and first suggests a drainage fault that the symptoms contradict. It also asks irrelevant questions, never suggests checking the belt or brushes, and ends by blaming the thermal cut-out, motor windings or PCB without evidence before advising replacement. Both give the stop-using warning, but Conversation 2's diagnosis is closer to the real cause and its advice is more useful.
